title: Not All Turns Are Equally Hard: Adaptive Thinking Budgets For Efficient Multi-Turn Reasoning in Agents
abstract: arXiv:2604.05164v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As LLM reasoning performance plateaus, improving inference-time compute efficiency is crucial to mitigate overthinking and long thinking traces even for simple queries. Prior approaches including length regularization, adaptive routing and difficulty-based budget allocation primarily focus on single-turn settings and fail to address the sequential dependencies inherent in multi-turn reasoning. We formulate multi-turn reasoning as a sequential compute allocation problem and model it as a multi-objective Markov Decision Process. We propose TAB: Turn-Adaptive Budgets, a budget allocation policy that takes as input the conversation history and learns to maximize task accuracy while respecting global per-problem token constraints, and consequently learns to adaptively allot smaller budgets to easier turns and save an appropriate number of tokens for the crucial harder reasoning steps. translated_title: 并非所有轮次都同样困难：面向智能体高效多轮推理的自适应思考预算
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）推理性能趋于瓶颈期，提升推理时计算效率变得至关重要，以缓解过度思考和冗长思考轨迹的问题，即使对于简单查询也是如此。先前的方法包括长度正则化、自适应路由和基于难度的预算分配，主要聚焦于单轮设置，未能解决多轮推理中固有的序列依赖性。我们将多轮推理形式化为一个序列计算分配问题，并将其建模为多目标马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）。我们提出了TAB：轮次自适应预算，这是一种预算分配策略，它以对话历史作为输入，学习在遵守每个问题的全局token约束的同时最大化任务准确率，从而学会自适应地为较容易的轮次分配更小的预算，并为关键的更困难推理步骤节省合适数量的token。我们在相应的数据集上训练并分析了TAB的行为。
tldr: 该论文提出轮次自适应预算策略TAB，将多轮推理建模为多目标马尔可夫决策过程，自适应地为简单轮次分配更少的思考token、为关键困难推理步骤保留预算，从而在遵守全局token约束的前提下提升智能体多轮推理的效率与准确率。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes TAB (Turn-Adaptive Budgets), a policy that formulates multi-turn reasoning as a multi-objective MDP and adaptively allocates smaller thinking budgets to easier turns while saving tokens for crucial harder reasoning steps, improving accuracy under global token constraints.
